title: People Hate Children
subtitle: I'm not a fan of trigger warnings, but this is an article about sexual assault.
body_html:
In other awful news, Abercrombie and Fitch’s former CEO was arrested today for charges that will strike residents of 2024 as a familiar theme:

Michael S. Jeffries, the former longtime chief executive of Abercrombie & Fitch, was indicted on Tuesday on charges of running an international sex-trafficking scheme during several years of his tenure at the company.

It’s a remarkably similar “playbook” for exploitation that we’ve seen from individuals like Harvey Weinstein, Jeffry Epstein, and (allegedly) Sean Combs. It’s similar to Bill Cosby. Being fabulously wealthy is not enough for some people. Predation on children and adults is how they choose to get through their day.

When I started my Child Psychiatry fellowship at Bellevue Hospital, I had a lecture with the now-deceased Dr. Schuyler Henderson. Week one of Child Psychiatry at NYU was Dr. Henderson telling us all in no uncertain terms—that people hate children. Children are routinely the victims of sexual abuse that would boil your soul away if you were to understand its scope and depravity.

I didn't understand what he meant at the time. He was the deputy director for child psychiatry at Bellevue Hospital. He later died by suicide. I think he understood things about the world that I wouldn’t learn until years later. The rest of us are only learning those details now. Some people are doing awful things to the most vulnerable people they can find. They are doing so regularly. Bill Cosby drugging people women till they were unconscious and then forcing himself on their unconscious bodies?

That wasn't just Bill. It was also (allegedly) Sean Combs; it was (allegedly) dozens of men in France; this kind of horrific violation is common.

Drugging people unconscious and raping them is normal for far too many people. For the attendees of Mr. Combs’ events, it was (allegedly) normalized. I think Schuyler knew this. I suspect it haunted him. Schuyler died by suicide about a year ago, and it still bothers me to think about it. We were not friends. He didn't like me, and I didn't particularly like him. I respected that he was Batman for the kids he served. Dr. Henderson got to hear the experiences of countless young people for himself. He was running an acute care setting for psychiatrically harmed children in the city of New York. The stories he heard? He learned what all child psychiatrists learn. Trauma is unbelievably pervasive. I've written about this before, noting that about 20% of girls will be sexually assaulted. And it's about 5% of boys. That is far too many children. Those children grow up.

Predatory individuals create emotionally toxic waste for the rest of the world. Many dysfunctional relationships are blamed on a mistrustful partner. Those are often people who were previously preyed upon. Every partner you've written off as “crazy?” Many of them learned to be “crazy” because they were victimized. They may have been those children mentioned above.

Trauma is toxic to the people who experienced it and to the other individuals who attempt to help them, or even interact with them, later. Trauma therapy is traumatic for the therapist. Trauma surgery is traumatic for the surgeons. The intensive care unit is traumatic for the staff. Inpatient psychiatric care is traumatic for both the patient and the nurses and staff. None of this is good. Hurt people hurt people. I imagine many of the index traumatizers had also been traumatized themselves. Finding “traumatizer zero” is not an easy task. What we very much need is less traumatized individuals.

And that means fewer people doing the traumatizing. And so here's where it gets tricky. Practically, if we don't take care of people who are violent or at risk of becoming violent, they're going to be violent. And they're going to participate in trauma and exploitation. We will all suffer in the aftermath. We also can't delude ourselves regarding how harmful trauma can be. This is true firsthand, and it's true secondhand. We don't have “oven mitts” yet for trauma therapists. We need to develop more occupational protections for those going into the emotional fire as treaters.

Predatory behavior is the modus operandi of many well-resourced individuals, and it happens for many years before anyone speaks out—observe the timelines related to the conduct of Mr. Combs. That latency between obvious predatory behavior and the whistle being blown? That's a social problem that we all need to take accountability for.

If there is one meaningful thing we can all advocate for, we need the courts to be faster. Individuals who've been traumatized are particularly vulnerable to not wanting to relive it. A court proceeding is as traumatic as it is prolonged. I've been harassed for many years and filed a lawsuit on April 11th, 2023, to address it. I'm still waiting for a judge to rule on even the first part of that case. These things take forever. At least I’m an adult, and I wasn’t preyed upon as a child, and I have a reserve to draw upon when the legal process drags on forever.

The edge predators have? They don't follow the law. They can swiftly take revenge, and people can learn not to cross them. Sean Combs is accused of firebombing Kid Cudi, who displeased him. People who want to allow legal processes to resolve their complaints? They are doomed to wait years even after they get the courage to file something. The delays in adjudication are themselves traumatizing.

Justice delayed is justice denied. It’s also more trauma-ensured. Appropriate resources for law enforcement and courts means the distance between predation and getting what’s coming to you might shrink enough for potential evil-doers to think twice. Or, better yet, victims will be allowed resolution sooner.

We’ve all had enough. The adjudication of allegations should be treated with the alacrity that the victims deserve.

Share
